doc.title: Rossano Sportiello interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 2, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Opening: Bach recording and St. Louis Blues with Nicki and Eddie
summary: Monk Rowe introduces the session at Fallcoming Jazz 2015 and mentions two recordings he heard, a Bach prelude and a wailing St. Louis Blues with the trio.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and we are actually in the Hampton Inn in New Hartford. I have Rossano Sportiello with me today on the occasion of Fallcoming Jazz 2015 at Hamilton College. Thanks for spending time with me.
It’s a pleasure and as we say in Italy, buongiorno.
I won’t try to say that because it won’t sound as good. Yesterday I was listening to two different recordings that you did. And on one you were playing “A Well-Tempered Clavier.” How do you say that?
Yeah, in Italian we say, “Un Clavicembalo ben temperato.” The Well-Tempered Clavier. Yeah. I recorded a prelude in one of my CDs, just as a piano solo.
That’s what I was listening to. And then I put on “The St. Louis Blues” that you did with Nicki and Eddie.
And you were wailing. And there was one part where it sounded like you were playing like the horn section in the Basie band.
So I was wondering if you like one better than the other.
